tools.name: lookup_disease
tools.description: Look up a specific canine inherited disease by name or OMIA id and return its governed record: canonical name, mode of inheritance, causal gene(s), OMIA curated description (summary / clinical features / molecular genetics / pathology), documented clinical signs (phenotype terms), the human OMIM analog, the count of peer-reviewed references + the landmark study, and the Mondo disease id. All sourced to OMIA (CC-BY). Returns a canonical sniff.world URL to cite. Dog-only.

query.description: A disease name (e.g. "degenerative myelopathy", "collie eye anomaly") or an OMIA id (e.g. "OMIA:001000-9615" or "263").

tools.name: search_diseases
tools.description: Search the canine disease catalogue by free text and return ranked candidate diseases (name + OMIA id + canonical sniff.world URL). Use this to find the exact disease before calling lookup_disease, or to enumerate diseases matching a term. Dog-only.

query.description: A disease name or fragment (e.g. "cataract", "von willebrand").

tools.name: lookup_canine_model
tools.description: Ask whether a human disease gene has a documented canine model foundation under Sniff's CoverageFrame (ortholog + ClinVar 3-star stack). Returns status answered | dark | not_in_universe. Dark answers include cause (unstudied | below_bar | unreachable | …), cause_definition, frame context counts, sources_checked, and as_of — never null/404. Gene symbol e.g. SOD1, TP53, BRCA2.

tools.name: agent_discover
tools.description: Cold-start orientation for agents: schema URL, release id, CoverageFrame list with fill rates, access modes (html/rest/mcp), tool names, license. Call once before deep work.

findings.title: Tool Chaining — 'search_diseases' directs LLM to call lookup_disease
findings.description: Tool 'search_diseases' description references tool(s) 'lookup_disease' from the same server using imperative language. This pattern can force an LLM into an unintended call chain or manufacture urgency to invoke a privileged tool.
findings.evidence: Search the canine disease catalogue by free text and return ranked candidate diseases (name + OMIA id + canonical sniff.world URL). Use this to find the exact disease before calling lookup_disease, or to enumerate diseases matching a term. Dog-only.
findings.remediation: Tool descriptions should describe what the tool does — not instruct the LLM on what other tools to call. Remove cross-tool directives and let the caller decide the execution order.

findings.title: Injection reflected — 'lookup_disease.query'
findings.description: Payload was echoed back as a named JSON field — likely input logging, not a vulnerability (field: sql).
findings.remediation: Sanitize and validate all input parameters. Never pass raw user input to shell commands, file paths, or SQL queries.

findings.title: Token Exposure — server version disclosure in HTTP response headers
findings.description: HTTP response header 'server: cloudflare' discloses internal information.
findings.remediation: Remove the 'server' response header in production.

findings.title: 'lookup_disease' accepts missing required fields
findings.description: Tool succeeded with empty arguments despite required: ['query']
findings.remediation: Validate that all required parameters are present before processing.

findings.title: 'lookup_disease.query' silently accepts wrong type
findings.description: Expected type 'string', sent NoneType value 'None' — no error returned.
findings.remediation: Validate parameter types strictly and return clear JSON-RPC errors on mismatch.

findings.title: 'search_diseases' accepts missing required fields
findings.description: Tool succeeded with empty arguments despite required: ['query']
findings.remediation: Validate that all required parameters are present before processing.

findings.title: initialize accepts protocol version downgrade
findings.description: The server accepted initialize with arbitrary protocol versions: ['9999-99-99', '2030-01-01', '1.0', '2024-01-01', '""']. The server also accepted far-future versions, indicating no version validation at all. Servers should reject versions outside their supported range to prevent feature-downgrade attacks.
findings.remediation: Validate protocolVersion against a supported range. Return a JSON-RPC error for versions outside that range.

findings.title: MCP server exposes tools with completable arguments
findings.description: 3 tool(s) have schema properties that may support completion/complete enumeration.
findings.remediation: Review which argument values are exposed via completion/complete.

findings.title: Server accepts path traversal cursor without validation
findings.description: tools/list accepted cursor='../../../../etc/passwd' and returned a result instead of rejecting it. This may indicate missing cursor validation.
findings.remediation: Validate cursor values; reject non-opaque or path-like cursor strings.
